title: No count in the search modal reads higher than 20
comment:
Tested on QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.8-d146c39, on 22 September 2026.
Re-measured at the moment of raising, on build v26.36.8-d146c39. One search for 'ZZ': the All tab reads All (111) while every tab for a single record type is correct and stops at 20 - Work orders (20), Customers (20), Assets (20), Parts (20), Vendors (11), Part sales (9), Purchase orders (6), Vendor invoices (5). 20+20+20+20+11+9+6+5 = 111, so the All figure is the per-type figures added together. A second search for 'ZZAUTOTEST' behaves the same way: All (61), which is 20+14+9+4+3+3+4+4. The same uncapped number is also read out to screen-reader users; that text is not visible on the screen. The requirement says no count in the box reads higher than 20, the tab included.
Not observed this run: The 'Show all N' links are absent on this build, so the third place the limit applies could not be read; that absence is already reported separately.
Raised as SV-10320 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10320 - with the marked-up picture and the requirement quoted word for word. It sits under the work covering wiring the search box up to the results, which is still with QA.
What needs to be done: nothing further from us. The report is with the developers under the link above, and this test is re-run once it is fixed.

title: Purchase Orders rank by Ordered status and recency
comment:
Tested on QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.8-d146c39, on 22 September 2026.
Re-checked on 22 September 2026, QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.8-d146c39, against requirements page 576978945 version 17. Measured on the screen. Still cannot be judged, and I have now proved it is the requirement rather than my effort. The requirement describes two states, still ordered and received, but the product has a middle one, Partial Delivery, that it never mentions. I searched the whole branch for a controlled pair - the same vendor, one still ordered, one fully received, with the received one NEWER so that age and state pull in opposite directions. No such pair exists in the data, and there is no way to set a purchase order's state directly: the only route to received is the full goods-receiving flow. Without knowing where a partly delivered order is meant to sit, the check has no answer even with a perfect fixture.
Not observed this run: Where a partly delivered purchase order is meant to rank.
Ask the product owner one question: does a partly delivered purchase order count as still ordered, or as received? The check can be judged the moment that is answered.

title: When two results are otherwise equal, the most recently updated one ranks first
comment:
Tested on QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.8-d146c39, on 21 September 2026.
Re-checked today on build v26.36.8-d146c39 with everything else held equal: two customers with the same name start, the same address, no jobs at all on either one, and both records opened first so neither counts as more recently looked at. The second one was changed, three times over 45 seconds the list was read, and the order never moved. A rename to the same record did show up in search within 15 seconds, so the search does notice changes to this record. HOWEVER: no customer record on this branch carries a 'last changed' date anywhere we can read, so it cannot be shown that one customer really is more recently updated than the other. 'The rule is not applied' and 'a customer has no date for the rule to read' look exactly the same from outside.
Not observed this run: Whether a customer record stores a last-changed time at all. No other record type on this branch both lacks its own recency scoring and shows a last-changed date, so the rule could not be re-tested elsewhere.
No report raised, on purpose - the question is with the QA lead. It cannot be proved the product was given a date to work with, so this goes to the product owner as a question instead of being raised as a fault.
What needs to be done: this is NOT being raised as a fault, because it cannot be proved the product was given anything to work with. It goes to the product owner as a question instead - does the most-recently-changed rule apply to customers at all, given customer records carry no dates? A near-identical report in this area was closed as not-a-defect three days ago, so this one waits for that answer.

title: Hovering a Work Order result shows an 'Add new line' action
comment:
Tested on QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.8-d146c39, on 21 September 2026.
No quick action appears on any search result row. Measured on the screen with a real mouse hover: two rounds over two queries (27 rows and 96 rows), 40 row-hovers in all, covering work orders, customers, assets, parts and vendors; then a second pass over 12 rows that watched the WHOLE page, not just the row, for any button appearing. Nothing appeared anywhere, and nothing appeared when the keyboard selection was moved either. The instrument is proved: every one of those hovers DID change the row on screen, and the same scan found 23 other buttons already on the page, so a quick action would have been seen. The owning story for this behaviour, SV-9173 (FE - Contextual quick actions on result rows), was read live in Jira on 21 September 2026 and its status is OBSOLETE, resolved Done. The story has been cancelled, so this cannot be judged as a product defect and no ticket is raised (Rule 112). The requirement is still written in the specification (page 576978945 version 17, section 8: 'show contextual quick actions on hover for each entity (desktop only)'), so the specification and the delivered scope now disagree. That disagreement is a question for the product owner, not a defect.
Ask the product owner whether contextual quick actions are dropped from this release. If they are dropped, the specification needs updating and these cases are retired. If they are not dropped, the cancelled story has to be reopened. Do not raise a defect while the owning story is cancelled.

The requirement is still written in the specification (page 576978945 version 17, section 8: 'show contextual quick actions on hover for each entity (desktop only)'), so the specification and the delivered scope now disagree. That disagreement is a question for the product owner, not a defect.
Ask the product owner whether contextual quick actions are dropped from this release. If they are dropped, the specification needs updating and these cases are retired. If they are not dropped, the cancelled story has to be reopened. Do not raise a defect while the owning story is cancelled.
